thread.title: S&P 500’s May rally attempt places major resistance under siege

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: S&P 500’s May rally attempt places major resistance under siege
text:
Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here.
Technically speaking, the major U.S. benchmarks have extended the May rally attempt, placing notable resistance under siege.
On a headline basis, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite have effectively nailed trendline resistance, and the prevailing retests, still underway, will likely set the near-term technical tone.
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, -0.26% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks.
As illustrated, the S&P has rallied to increasingly familiar resistance.
Monday’s close (2,672.6) matched the 2017 close (2,673) and registered slightly under the 50-day moving average, currently 2,679.
This area more broadly matches trendline resistance pinned to the March peak.
Similarly, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has rallied to the range top.
Here again, the index remains capped by the 50-day moving average, currently 24,440.
On further strength, additional resistance (24,526) matches the bottom of the March gap.
Meanwhile, the Nasdaq Composite’s near-term backdrop remains stronger.
As illustrated, the index has reclaimed the 50-day moving average, reaching nearly three-week highs.
The breakout originates from the 2017 peak — roughly, the 7,000 mark — and opens the path to major resistance, better illustrated below.
Widening the view to six months adds perspective.
On this wider view, the Nasdaq has reached a notable technical test.
Consider that significant resistance matches three areas, detailed previously:
Trendline resistance closely matching the April closing peak of 7,295. The absolute April peak of 7,319. Resistance matching the March gap, spanning from 7,303 to 7,325. Combined, resistance broadly spans from about 7,295 to 7,325.
Monday’s session high (7,292) closely matched resistance, and the retest remains underway.
An eventual close higher would negate the Nasdaq’s developing head-and-shoulders top. This is a bearish pattern defined by the January, March and April peaks.
Looking elsewhere, the Dow Jones Industrial Average is rising from major support.
Consider that the May low (23,531), established Thursday, effectively matched the Dow’s 2018 closing low (23,533).
The subsequent rally from support punctuates a second successful test of the 200-day moving average.
Additional overhead broadly spans from the 50-day moving average, currently 24,440, to the 2017 close (24,719).
Similarly, the S&P 500 has staged a bullish reversal, rising from last week’s shaky, but successful, test of the 200-day moving average.
Recall that trendline resistance closely matches the 2017 close (2,673). To reiterate, Monday’s close (2,672.6) matched resistance, and the retest remains underway.
The bigger picture As detailed above, the U.S. benchmarks’ prevailing rally attempt has placed significant technical tests in play.
On a headline basis, the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 have effectively nailed well-defined trendlines, and the prevailing retests, across the next several sessions, should be a useful bull-bear gauge.
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF IWM, +0.20% remains the strongest widely-tracked U.S. benchmark, in the broad sweep.
Still, the IWM is traversing a jagged six-month range. The 2017 peak (155.41) effectively bisects the prevailing range, and the small-cap benchmark has ticked higher amid decreased volume.
Meanwhile, the S&P MidCap 400 is pressing trendline resistance, circa 347.
On further strength, additional overhead spans from 349.16 to 349.75, levels matching the 2017 peak and the April closing peak. An eventual close higher would strengthen the bull case.
Against this backdrop, the S&P 500’s pending technical tests remain relatively straightforward.
To start, major S&P 500 resistance broadly spans from 2,673 to 2,695, levels matching the 2017 close and the 2017 peak.
This area also matches trendline resistance and the 50-day moving average, currently 2,679. A close higher would mark progress.
On further strength, more distant resistance (2,710) closely matches the top of the March gap and the April closing peak. An eventual close higher would mark a “higher high” more firmly signaling a trend shift.
Beyond specific levels, the bigger picture technicals remain bearish-leaning based on today’s backdrop.
Market rally attempts have been fueled by lackluster volume and breadth against the backdrop of less-than-ideal sector participation. (For instance, energy and large-cap technology have paced recent strength amid lackluster transports and financials participation.)
The pending tests of trendline resistance may add color.
See also: Charting a bearish market backdrop as seasonal headwind (May) kicks off.
Tuesday’s Watch List The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library.
Drilling down further, the iShares China Large-Cap ETF FXI, +1.21% remains tenuously positioned.
Recall that major support matches the range bottom, technically spanning from about 45.50 to 46.00.
This area roughly matches the 200-day moving average, currently 46.50.
Last week’s low (45.65) closely matched major support, and the retest remains underway.
More broadly, the shares are threatening to resolve a bearish descending triangle with a downside break. Consider that Monday marked the first close under the 200-day moving average since January 4, 2017.
Conversely, trendline resistance closely tracks the 50-day moving average, currently 47.35. An eventual close higher would strengthen the backdrop
Meanwhile, the iShares Europe ETF IEV, -0.29% remains relatively stronger, though the prevailing backdrop does not scream “raging bull.”
The shares initially spiked four weeks ago, clearing the 200- and 50-day moving averages, and ultimately reaching three-month highs. (The “higher high” combined with the rally atop the trending indicators is consistent with a trend shift.)
By comparison, the ensuing pullback has been flat, underpinned by the major moving averages.
Tactically, the 50-day moving average has marked an inflection point, and the recovery attempt is intact barring a violation.
Moving to specific names, Tableau Software, Inc. DATA, +2.10% is a well positioned large-cap name.
As illustrated, the shares have recently gapped to two-year highs, rising after the company’s strong first-quarter results.
The subsequent pullback has been comparably flat, underpinned by the top of the gap. Deeper support matches the breakout point, circa 87.50, and a sustained posture higher supports a firmly bullish bias.
Coupa Software, Inc. COUP, +2.87% is a mid-cap name positioned to rise.
Technically, the shares are challenging a two-month range top, tagging a nominal all-time high this week.
The May upturn has been fueled by increased volume — and comes from a tight range, underpinned by the 50-day moving average — laying the groundwork for a potentially more decisive breakout. A near-term target projects to the 53 area on follow-through.
PulteGroup, Inc. PHM, +0.02% is a large-cap homebuilder showing signs of life.
Late last month, the shares rallied to the range top, rising on increased volume after the company’s quarterly results.
The shares have subsequently held tightly to resistance, closely matching the 100-day moving average, improving the chances of eventual follow-through.
Tactically, near-term support matches the May low (30.20) and a breakout attempt is in play barring a violation.
Now, Inc. DNOW, +0.42% is a mid-cap oil services name.
Earlier this month, the shares knifed to nine-month highs, rising after the company’s first-quarter results. The breakout punctuated a bull flag, underpinned by the 200-day moving average.
Though still near-term extended, and due to consolidate, the nearly straightline strong-volume spike is longer-term bullish. Tactically, near-term support (13.80) is followed by the deeper breakout point (13.00).
